Protocols / Phenotyping & imaging

Measuring cell volume

Phenotyping & imagingBy Various authorsVersion 1 · updated 2026-10-07

Crushing clusters to a single layer, then Calcofluor staining and imaging to estimate cell volume as an ellipsoid.

Download (.docx) PDF

Adapted from the lab compendium Snowflake Yeast Protocols — Ratcliff Lab / MuLTEE (V2).

  1. Transfer 25 μL of culture to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
  2. Macroscopic strains: sample using 100 μL wide-bore tips, then break clusters into small pieces using 100 μL regular-bore tips to facilitate single-layer crushing later (see Crushing clusters › Breaking up and crushing clusters: collected methods).
  3. Pellet clusters (5,000 × g, 1 min), wash with 1 mL 1× PBS.
  4. Stain in 100 μL of 5 μM Calcofluor White in 1× PBS at room temperature.
  5. Crush 5 μL of stained clusters into a single layer of cells between a slide and coverslip, without shearing.
  6. Image on a Nikon Eclipse Ti inverted microscope, brightfield and UV/fluorescent channels, ≥5 fields of view per strain at ×40 magnification. Set focus in brightfield to the plane where cells appear grey, then move down 0.7 μm for sharp fluorescent cell-wall signal.
  7. Cell volume is calculated as an ellipsoid: V = 4/3 × πab², where a and b are the major- and minor-axis lengths measured from segmented cells.

Image analysis pipeline (cell segmentation): same pipeline as Phenotyping & imaging › Measuring cell aspect ratio.
